title: Expression-bodied members
hook: A Redis key builder that is one interpolation does not need a brace block — expression-bodied members are the language's way of saying the body is a single expression.

sections.heading: => on members is not a lambda
sections.prose: Expression-bodied members use the same => token as lambdas, but they are ordinary methods, properties, constructors, finalizers, and indexers whose body is one expression. The compiler still emits a member. You cannot declare a local function inside an expression-bodied member. Use a block body the moment you need statements, more than a trivial guard, or a local function. C# 14 field-backed properties can mix an expression-bodied accessor with the field keyword; that is still a property, not a lambda.

snippets.label: Cache keys as expression-bodied members
snippets.explanation: Methods, get-only properties, and constructors can all be expression-bodied. The constructor form runs the expression as the body after the initializer list.

sections.heading: When a block is clearer
sections.prose: Interviewers are not grading you for maximum => density. A switch expression as the entire method body is fair. Two cache writes and a return are a block. Mixing an expression-bodied get with a block set is legal and common. Do not hide await in a one-liner that logs, mutates, and returns; the reader cannot see sequencing.

snippets.label: Switch expression as a method body
snippets.explanation: This is both an expression-bodied member and a switch expression. Exhaustiveness is the compiler's job; the discard throws instead of inventing a TTL.

interviewTakeaways: => on a member is a body form, not a delegate conversion.
Allowed on methods, properties, operators, constructors, indexers, finalizers.
Local functions cannot be declared inside an expression-bodied member.
Prefer a block when sequencing or locals matter.
commonPitfalls: Calling a one-line => method a lambda in an interview.
Stuffing statements into a ternary to keep the expression body.
Forgetting that expression-bodied constructors still run initializers first.

jsTsCorrelations.note: class C { foo = () => this.x } is a field holding an arrow, which is a different this model. C# expression-bodied members are still instance methods with a real this.
